new_statements.translation: [Table 7, 20th-century column, Wahkowa 'resguardo de Angosturas', Phonology:] The phonological system of the language consists of 12 consonantal and 10 vocalic segments, five oral and five nasal. [...] Accent: contrastive, oppositive, free. [17th-century column: Accent: accent is not marked in the 17th-century documents.] [...] Morpheme: thematic, vocative. {-a} theme, {-o,-u} vocative: abá 'mother' ... abú, abó 'mother' (vocative); koʃa 'brother', koʃó 'brother' (vocative); bisría fem. name, bisriú vocative; sirina masc. name ... sirinu vocative.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent in the Uwa of Angosturas is phonemically contrastive and free: its position is not fixed or predictable and distinguishes words; it is therefore marked lexically (author writes acute accents, e.g. abá 'mother', bisría; vocative suffix -o/-u attracts the accent: koʃa -> koʃó).
new_statements.exceptions: None discussed; the only pattern visible in the examples is that the vocative forms in -o/-u carry final accent (abú/abó, koʃó, bisriú). Author also notes /m,p,b/ and /l,r,d/ alternate according to speaker origin within the resguardo (mixed-origin community).
new_statements.domain_note: One-line entry in a phonology summary table based on the author's own field data from Angosturas (isolated words: toponyms, anthroponyms, kin terms); word-level, citation forms. No discussion of phrase-level prosody. Consistent with Headland 1997:16 for Central Tunebo ('lengua no-tonal en que el acento prosodico tiene significado: wíquinro/wiquínro, ába/abá').
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is explicitly for the Uwa spoken in Wahkowa, 'resguardo de Angosturas', municipio de Tame (Arauca) -- i.e. exactly Angosturas Tunebo [tnd], ango1257 -- based on Casilimas Rojas's own fieldwork there (her other papers label the variety 'Variante Angosturas, TAME (Arauca)'). She notes the resguardo has speakers 'de diferentes origenes' (some phoneme alternations by speaker origin). The Headland 1997 statement examined for comparison describes Central Tunebo (Cobaria/Tegria, cent2150), and Marquez et al. 1988 describes Cobaria; neither is Angosturas.

sources.note: p. 16 (Central Tunebo, not Angosturas): 'La palabra fonologica consta de dos a cinco silabas en una unidad secuencial marcada por un nucleo. El nucleo es la silaba que recibe mayor fuerza intensiva.. El uw cuwa es una lengua no-tonal en que el acento prosodico tiene significado: wiquinro 'yo doy', wiquinro 'yo vengo', aba 'sangre' aba 'madre'' (accent marks distinguish the pairs) -- contrastive/lexical stress.
